doc:
**Finite comparison.** Paired samples `q n ≡ p n + r n (mod 1)` have discrepancies within
`E/N + 2ε`, where `E` counts the positions with `|r n| ≥ ε`. This is Phase 18's

name: NormalityChecker.AdditionSpectrum.sampleDisc_compare

doc:
**Mixture of a retired and an active part.** If the retired positions carry the model

lies between the retired proportion and the retired proportion plus `H/N`.
label: sampleDisc_mixture
name: NormalityChecker.AdditionSpectrum.sampleDisc_mixture

doc:
**Block Cesàro lemma.** Suppose consecutive blocks `[S k, S (k+1))` have lengths negligible
against their starts, and that a family of functions bounded by one has block sums that are
eventually a vanishing proportion of the block lengths, uniformly in the family. Then all
prefix sums are `o(N)`, uniformly in the family.
label: block_cesaro
name: NormalityChecker.AdditionSpectrum.block_cesaro

label: prefix_state

programmed numbers is the shifted form of the states plus an integer plus the shifted tails.
label: form_pairing
name: NormalityChecker.AdditionSpectrum.form_pairing

doc:
**Segment count.** A segment of `M p^ρ` periods of the orbit of `A / p^(v+g)`, where
`A = p^ρ a'` with `a'` a unit and `ρ ≤ g`, has interval counting error at most `t p^ρ M`.

name: NormalityChecker.AdditionSpectrum.mixtureRealizable

doc:
**Exact involution cancellation for odd periodic Dirichlet convolutions (Track B3).**
If `f` is odd `M`-periodic, `p` is prime with `M ∣ p + 1`, `n ≠ 0`, and `v_p(n)` is odd,
then `(1 * f)(n) = 0`.
label: dirichletOneConv_eq_zero_of_odd_padicVal
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.dirichletOneConv_eq_zero_of_odd_padicVal

doc: Exact divisor-counting identity `∑_{n=1}^X τ(n) = ∑_{d=1}^X ⌊X / d⌋`.
label: sum_card_divisors_eq
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.sum_card_divisors_eq

doc: Elementary harmonic bound: `∑_{d=1}^X 1/d ≤ 1 + log X` for `X ≥ 1`.
label: harmonic_sum_le_one_add_log
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.harmonic_sum_le_one_add_log

doc:
**Logarithmic aggregate mass bound for bounded Dirichlet convolutions (Tracks B3–B4).**
If `|f(m)| ≤ B` for all `m`, then `absMass (dirichletOneConv f) X ≤ 2 * B * X * log(X + 2)`.
label: absMass_dirichletOneConv_le
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.absMass_dirichletOneConv_le

doc:
Exact Lambert-to-Dirichlet expansion of a residue-class Lambert sum:
`∑' k, 1 / (b^(k*M + r) - 1) = ∑' n, (#{d ∣ n : d % M = r}) / b^n`.
label: residueLambert_eq_coeffSeries
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.residueLambert_eq_coeffSeries

doc:
**Exact antisymmetric residue-class Lambert identity (Track B3).**
For every radix `b ≥ 2`, modulus `M ≥ 2`, and `1 ≤ r < M`,
`A_{r, M}(b) - A_{M - r, M}(b) = coeffSeries b (dirichletOneConv (antiIndicator M r))`.
label: residueLambert_sub_eq_coeffSeries
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.residueLambert_sub_eq_coeffSeries

doc:
**Exact `q`-digamma reflection to Dirichlet series identity (Track B4).**
At `q = b^(-M)`,
`(ψ_q(r/M) - ψ_q(1 - r/M)) / log q = coeffSeries b (dirichletOneConv (antiIndicator M r))`.
label: qDigamma_reflection_eq_dirichletSeries
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.qDigamma_reflection_eq_dirichletSeries

doc:
**Conditional-on-sparsity `K_b` transfer for bounded Dirichlet convolutions (Track B3).**
If `|f m| ≤ B` for all `m` and `supportCount (dirichletOneConv f) N * log(log(N + 3)) / N → 0`,
then `D_N(coeffSeries b (dirichletOneConv f); b) → 1` for every radix `b ≥ 2`.
label: bounded_dirichletOneConv_tendsto_one_of_sparse
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.bounded_dirichletOneConv_tendsto_one_of_sparse

doc:
**`q`-digamma reflection `K_b` transfer (Track B4).**
Given the analytic support bound `S(N) * log(log(N + 3)) / N → 0` for
`dirichletOneConv (antiIndicator M r)` (which vanishes at every `n` with odd `v_p(n)` for
any prime `p ≡ -1 (mod M)` by `dirichletOneConv_eq_zero_of_odd_padicVal`), the normalized
`q`-digamma reflection difference at `q = b^(-M)` has limiting base-`b` discrepancy `1` and
preserves discrepancy under translation.
label: qDigamma_reflection_tendsto_one_of_sparse
name: NormalityChecker.AntisymmetricLambert.qDigamma_reflection_tendsto_one_of_sparse

doc:
For normalized observations, uniform estimates through frequency `H-1`
give a bound for every interval and every partial cell. The grid width `w`
and the model tolerance `δ` can be chosen independently.
label: approximate_interval_count_bound
name: NormalityChecker.approximate_interval_count_bound

doc: A separate integral shift can be removed at each sample.
label: phase_model_sum_bound
name: NormalityChecker.phase_model_sum_bound

Finite-cutoff Weyl bound with separate costs for model cancellation, mean
error in turns, exceptional full blocks, and the final partial block.
label: approximate_prefix_bound
name: NormalityChecker.approximate_prefix_bound

A good block can use any smooth rational orbit whose mean phase distance is
small. Its initial rational value may be chosen independently on each block.
label: normal_of_approximate_arithmetic_certificate
name: NormalityChecker.normal_of_approximate_arithmetic_certificate

doc:
Sufficient conditions on rational prefixes. At every fixed denominator cutoff
`M`, the exceptional starts may include insertions, clearing delays and severe
cancellations. The polynomial exponent is fixed across all cutoffs and scales.
label: normal_of_arithmetic_certificate
name: NormalityChecker.normal_of_arithmetic_certificate

doc: A unique summand with a pole at `p` forces a pole in the reduced sum.
label: unique_prime_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.unique_prime_denominator

Primes in the top half with residue `1` or `5` modulo eight survive in the
uncorrected shifted prefix (including the coefficient at `n`).
label: prefix_upper_prime
name: NormalityChecker.BBP.prefix_upper_prime

doc: This integral evaluates the BBP sum without an external axiom for its value.
label: integral_pi
name: NormalityChecker.BBP.integral_pi

label: shadow_integral
name: NormalityChecker.BBP.shadow_integral

label: shadow_error
name: NormalityChecker.BBP.shadow_error

label: shadow_error_after_shifts
name: NormalityChecker.BBP.shadow_error_after_shifts

label: not_normal_of_frequent_excess
name: NormalityChecker.not_normal_of_frequent_excess

doc: A finite-sample bound for arbitrary half-open intervals, valid from N=2.
label: discrepancy_le_transitions
name: NormalityChecker.discrepancy_le_transitions

doc:
If a shift is outside the two constant-word cylinders of length k+2,
one of its next k+1 positions is a transition.
label: transition_near_interior
name: NormalityChecker.transition_near_interior

doc:
Counting positions that can reach a marked position within k further
steps. The last k starts account for the finite-prefix boundary.
label: count_within_steps
name: NormalityChecker.count_within_steps

doc:
Positive lower transition density is exactly the condition that the upper
limiting discrepancy is strictly below one.
label: discrepancy_lt_one_iff_transitions
name: NormalityChecker.discrepancy_lt_one_iff_transitions

doc: The diagonal model retains `p` precisely when a truncated binomial sum is nonzero modulo `p`.
label: logShadow_binomial_prime
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_binomial_prime

doc: Averages at ends of complete scales, for cells with prescribed limiting means.
label: mean_at_scale
name: NormalityChecker.mean_at_scale

doc: A single modular orbit approximates the entire finite sum on a scale cell.
label: cell_orbit_approx
name: NormalityChecker.cell_orbit_approx

The insertion depths are constant offsets from the scale k throughout a cell.
The last inequality allows the next insertion at the upper endpoint.
label: cell_cancellation
name: NormalityChecker.cell_cancellation

The computed fraction bounds the number of uncontrolled positions before
*every* cutoff. Cells below the first scale carry no charge.

name: NormalityChecker.CellProfile.count_bound

doc: Full blocks suffice. The final partial block costs at most `B` at every cutoff.
label: prefix_block_bound
name: NormalityChecker.prefix_block_bound

A geometric cell contains `L^k` full blocks of length `B^k`. Both the relative
size of the exceptional set and the normalized sums on its complement may be made
arbitrarily small, separately for each fixed Fourier frequency.
label: normal_of_sparse_blocks
name: NormalityChecker.normal_of_sparse_blocks

doc:
Short and long zero shells have different discrepancies, even though their
grouped zero indicators are both the alternating word 1010….
label: alternating_ratio_discrepancies
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.alternating_ratio_discrepancies

doc:
**Radix shift invariance of finite extreme discrepancy.**
For every integer radix `b`, real `x`, `k : ℕ`, and `N > 0`,
`|D_N(b^k x; b) - D_N(x; b)| ≤ k / N`.
label: radixDiscrepancy_mul_pow_sub_le
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.radixDiscrepancy_mul_pow_sub_le

doc:
`discDist` of a finite integer linear combination from `0` is bounded by the weighted sum
of individual deficits `1 - D_N(z_i)`.
label: discDist_sum_intMul_le
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.discDist_sum_intMul_le

doc:
**General power-of-radix linear discrepancy transfer.**
If `b^k x - y = ∑ i ∈ s, c_i z_i` with integer coefficients `c_i`, then for every `N > 0`,
`|D_N(x; b) - D_N(y; b)| ≤ k / N + ∑ i ∈ s, |c_i| · (1 - D_N(z_i; b))`.
label: radix_pow_linear_transfer
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.radix_pow_linear_transfer

doc: Summability of `binaryLambert w` for any bounded weight `|w(m)| ≤ B`.
label: summable_binaryLambert
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.summable_binaryLambert

doc: Exact mod-8 character-orthogonality identities for `4 A_r - E_odd` (`r ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}`).
label: mod8_character_identities
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.mod8_character_identities

doc:
**Finite mod-8 transfer to the odd-index Erdős–Borwein sum (Track E1).**
For every `r ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}` and every `N > 0`,
`|D_N(A_r; 2) - D_N(E_odd; 2)| ≤ 2/N + (1 - D_N(L_{χ₄}; 2)) + (1 - D_N(L_{χ₈}; 2)) + (1 - D_N(L_{χ_{-8}}; 2))`.
label: mod8_odd_discrepancy_diff
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.mod8_odd_discrepancy_diff

doc:
**Pairwise mod-8 residue-class discrepancy transfer (Track E1).**
For every `r, s ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}` and `N > 0`,
`|D_N(A_r; 2) - D_N(A_s; 2)| ≤ 4/N + 2·((1 - D_N(L_{χ₄})) + (1 - D_N(L_{χ₈})) + (1 - D_N(L_{χ_{-8}})))`.
label: mod8_class_discrepancy_diff
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.mod8_class_discrepancy_diff

doc:
**Asymptotic discrepancy equivalence of mod-8 Lambert classes and `E_odd` (Track E1).**
Given `D_N(L_{χ}; 2) → 1` for the three nonprincipal real characters mod 8 (established in
Phase 17 / Paper VI), all four `A_r` (`r ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}`) and `E_odd` have asymptotically
identical binary discrepancy: `D_N(A_r; 2) - D_N(E_odd; 2) → 0`.
label: mod8_asymptotic_equivalence
name: NormalityChecker.CharacterLambertTransfer.mod8_asymptotic_equivalence

doc: Uniform error for the actual logarithm, using one polynomial of exact degree d.
label: full_degree_log_error
name: NormalityChecker.full_degree_log_error

The integral `∑_{k < D} Q k / (k + 1)` of an integer polynomial of degree `< D`
has reduced denominator dividing `lcmRange D`.
label: poly_integral_den_dvd_lcmRange
name: NormalityChecker.ChebyshevPoleApproximation.poly_integral_den_dvd_lcmRange

doc:
After dividing by `2^w`, the shifted rational `Y_N = -2^{-w} ∫_0^1 Q_D(x) dx`
has reduced denominator dividing `2^w * lcmRange D`.
label: shifted_poly_integral_den_dvd
name: NormalityChecker.ChebyshevPoleApproximation.shifted_poly_integral_den_dvd

doc:
Rounding error bound on `[0, 1]`: if `|Q k - R k| ≤ 1/2` for all `k < D`, then
`|∑_{k < D} Q k / (k + 1) - ∑_{k < D} R k / (k + 1)| ≤ (1/2) ∑_{k < D} 1 / (k + 1)`.
label: rounding_integral_error
name: NormalityChecker.ChebyshevPoleApproximation.rounding_integral_error

doc:
Master error bound for the single-pole (`1/(1+x)`) rounded Chebyshev-pole approximant:
given the exact pole identity `2^e ln 2 + ∫_0^1 R_D = (2^e / T(-1)) ∫_0^1 T(x)/(1+x) dx`,
`|∫_0^1 T(x)/(1+x) dx| ≤ ln 2`, and `|Q_k - R_k| ≤ 1/2` for all `k < D`, the integer-polynomial
integral `∫_0^1 Q_D(x) dx = ∑_{k < D} Q_k / (k + 1)` approximates `-2^e ln 2` within
`(2^e / |T(-1)|) ln 2 + (1/2) H_D`.

Closed count at every cell boundary. Its bounded offset from the periodic

doc:

for some integer `z : ℤ`.

name: NormalityChecker.NormalReciprocalCore.band_identity

doc:
**Proposition D2.5 (exact alternating-sign band identity).**
With `+` in place of `-`, on every band `i` the leading multiplier is `1` for even `i` and `0`
for odd `i`, so odd bands concentrate near `0 mod 1`.

name: NormalityChecker.NormalReciprocalCore.signed_band_identity

doc:

name: NormalityChecker.NormalReciprocalCore.sum_residues_cexp_eq_zero

doc:

label: eulerAutomaton_purely_periodic
name: NormalityChecker.NormalReciprocalCore.eulerAutomaton_purely_periodic

The denominator at the midpoint is constant up to the next power of two.

Extreme interval discrepancy at ordinary prefixes, including endpoints
inside an exceptional upper half.

name: NormalityChecker.ParameterTwoQuadratic.quadratic_discrepancy_limits

Harmonic weights on digit positions give the correct length for every
interval, without a growth or algebraicity hypothesis.

name: NormalityChecker.ParameterTwoQuadratic.quadratic_log_equidistribution

label: square_normal

doc:
The congruence for the rational weighted sum, with its odd denominator
explicitly cleared on both sides.
label: weighted_congruence
name: NormalityChecker.ParameterTwoSquare.weighted_congruence

After clearing the radix, the missing-diagonal difference contains exactly

name: NormalityChecker.ParameterTwoSquare.diagonal_numerator

Reduced numerator and denominator before the midpoint. Here `k` is

At and after the midpoint the reduced numerator is the odd quotient of

doc: All cutoffs, including the empty prefix before the first pair at four.
label: exact_profile
name: NormalityChecker.ParameterTwoSquare.exact_profile

doc: Any positive integer mesh size can be used, including `q=b^k` for a digit test.
label: discrepancy_of_fixed_cells
name: NormalityChecker.discrepancy_of_fixed_cells

doc:
`G N` may vary with the prefix. A uniformly distributed selected part covering
at least `g` in lower density bounds the full asymptotic discrepancy by `1-g`.
label: discrepancy_of_uniform_share
name: NormalityChecker.discrepancy_of_uniform_share

doc: A cycle witness exists even when `p` shares factors with the coefficient period.
label: exists_power_cycle
name: NormalityChecker.exists_power_cycle

doc: Complete test at order one. `J,L` can be any certified preperiod and cycle length.
label: periodic_normal_iff_phases
name: NormalityChecker.periodic_normal_iff_phases

doc: One recurring phase is exactly zero in this dense binary expansion.
label: signed_four_nonnormal
name: NormalityChecker.signed_four_nonnormal

doc:
For a nonempty cycle of roots of unity and `c > 2`, every complex conjugate of the
geometric value has absolute value strictly between zero and one. Thus it is nonintegral.
label: periodicGeometricValue_not_isIntegral
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.periodicGeometricValue_not_isIntegral

doc:
For all sufficiently large boxes, their mass is a monic polynomial in the
one-dimensional partial sum. The polynomial is independent of the box size.
label: upper_box_monic_polynomial
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.upper_box_monic_polynomial

doc:
If integral coordinate weights sum to a nonintegral element, every nonempty upper
set has a nonzero limiting mass. This applies in the p-adic field with integrality over ℤ.
label: upper_box_nonzero_limit
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.upper_box_nonzero_limit

doc:
For a periodic cycle of roots of unity from a number field, the mass of every
nonempty upper set has a nonzero limit in any complete normed field where `‖c‖ < 1`.
label: periodic_upper_mass_nonzero
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.periodic_upper_mass_nonzero

doc:
After removing the radix unit and clearing the common denominator, the actual
rational prefix agrees with the reflected box mass to the prescribed p-adic precision.
label: reflected_prefix_error
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.reflected_prefix_error

doc:
For every prime divisor of the parameter, the prefix of a power of a
single axis retains the full expected pole order up to a bounded loss.
label: periodic_power_retained_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.periodic_power_retained_denominator

doc:
Every nonconstant rational polynomial of the positive-index Stoneham number
is normal in base `b` for coprime `b ≥ 2` and `c > 2`.
label: coprime_polynomial_normal
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.coprime_polynomial_normal

doc: Simultaneous rectangle frequencies for distinct powers of any generator with c > 2.
label: coprime_joint_powers
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.coprime_joint_powers

doc:
Nonzero limits for individual upper sets give a single precision valid for
all upper sets through the anchor, at every larger box size and precision.
label: uniform_padic_box_precision
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.uniform_padic_box_precision

doc:
The reflected inverse radix agrees at precision `p^L` with one of finitely
many periodic cycles. Each cycle has a nonzero limiting mass on every nonempty upper set.
label: exists_reflected_cycles
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.exists_reflected_cycles

doc:
For an unrestricted period, the sparse boundary may visit many residues.
A single nonzero amplitude occurring infinitely often among zero amplitudes suffices.
label: periodic_mask_normal
name: NormalityChecker.periodic_mask_normal

doc:
For a period dividing `c-1`, the rational sum of one discounted period
starting at class one decides between exact zero and base-`b` normality.
label: periodic_plateau_test
name: NormalityChecker.periodic_plateau_test

doc: Refining the precision can only shrink the failed subset of the phase interval.
label: failed_region_antitone
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.failed_region_antitone

doc:
With a single off-base prime at order one, the true extreme interval discrepancy
is the maximum of the prefix score of the persistent cancellation set on `[1,p]`.
label: discrepancy_eq_persistent_max
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.discrepancy_eq_persistent_max

doc: Digit normality is equivalent to Lebesgue-null persistent failure.
label: normal_iff_persistent_null
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.normal_iff_persistent_null

doc:
Closed-form sum formula for `quadZ b j`:
`Z_{j+1} = 1 - 2^(j+1) * b^(2^(j+1)) + ∑_{i=0}^j 2^(j - i) * b^(2^(j+1) - 2^(i+1))`.
label: quadZ_closed_form
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.quadZ_closed_form

doc:
Exact 2-adic link between `quadZ b j` and Phase 14's `cancellation b j` (= `T_{j+1}`):
in `ℚ_[2]`, `quadZ b j = 2^(j+1) * b^(2^(j+1)) * cancellation b j`!
Since `b` is odd, `‖b^(2^(j+1))‖₂ = 1`, so `v₂(quadZ b j) = (j + 1) + v₂(T_{j+1})`.
label: quadZ_eq_cancellation
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.quadZ_eq_cancellation

doc:
Exact upper-shell denominator formula for `X^2 - 2X` in terms of `quadZ`:
on `3 * 2^j ≤ n < 2^(j+2)`, `den(prefix b n 1 (-2) C₀) = max 1 (2^(2*j+1) * ‖quadZ b j‖₂)`.
label: quadratic_upper_den_eq_quadZ
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.quadratic_upper_den_eq_quadZ

doc:
Exact single-shape maximum relative length for the primary corner `(1, 1)` of
`α_{2,3} α_{2,5}`: for every positive ratio `r = Q/P > 0`,
`min(4r/5, 2/3) / (1 + r) ≤ 4/11`, with equality at `r = 5/6`.
label: single_shape_one_one_max
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.single_shape_one_one_max

doc:
Exact piecewise-linear boundary-strip upper bound for base `p > 1`, `0 < η < 1`,
`p * η ≤ p - 1` (e.g. `p ≥ 2` and `η ≤ 1/2`), and `0 < t`:
`min(1 - t, (η / (1 - η)) * t) + (η / ((p - 1) * (1 - η))) * t ≤ (p / (p - 1)) * η`.
label: boundary_strip_piecewise_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.boundary_strip_piecewise_le

doc:
Simultaneous ultrametric separation for active shells of the same nonrectangular shape:
if two distinct shells `(K₁, L₁)` and `(K₂, L₂)` with `L₁ < L₂` and `K₁ < K₂` agree with the
same target classes modulo `2 * 3^(h - 1)` and `4 * 5^(k - 1)`, then
`L₂ - L₁ ≥ 2 * 3^(h - 1)` and `K₂ - K₁ ≥ 4 * 5^(k - 1)`.
label: simultaneous_ultrametric_spacing
name: NormalityChecker.Phase16StonehamBounds.simultaneous_ultrametric_spacing

doc:
Lower discrepancy gap in terms of adjacent binary transitions (`01` and `10`):
for every real `x` and `N ≥ 1`, `min (1/3) (transitionFrequency x N) - 1/N ≤ 1 - binaryDiscrepancy x N`.
label: one_sub_discrepancy_ge_transition
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.one_sub_discrepancy_ge_transition

doc:
If `shift 2 x n ≥ 2⁻ᴸ` (`L ≥ 1`), then some position `n + j` with `j ≤ L - 1` has a `1`-bit
(`shift 2 x (n + j) ≥ 1/2`).
label: nonzero_shift_has_one_bit
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.nonzero_shift_has_one_bit

doc:
Frequency of shifts in `[2⁻ᴸ, 1)` is controlled by `L` times the `1`-bit frequency plus
the boundary allowance `(L - 1) / N`.
label: upper_freq_le_one_bits
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.upper_freq_le_one_bits

doc:
Upper discrepancy gap in terms of the `1`-bit frequency: for every real `x`, `L ≥ 1`, and `N ≥ 1`,
`1 - binaryDiscrepancy x N ≤ (1/2)^L + (L - 1)/N + L * frequency (shift 2 x) (1/2) 1 N`.
Optimizing `L = ⌈(1/2) log₂(log N)⌉` when the `1`-bit frequency is `O(1 / √(log N))` yields
`1 - D_N(x) = O((log log N) / √(log N))`.
label: one_sub_discrepancy_le_one_bits
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.one_sub_discrepancy_le_one_bits

doc:
Lower discrepancy gap from two separated positive-mass intervals `[0, ε)` and `[3ε, 1/2)`:
if `0 < ε ≤ 1/6`, `Δ ≤ ε`, and both `[0, ε)` and `[3ε, 1/2)` receive empirical frequency at least `Δ`,
then `Δ ≤ 1 - binaryDiscrepancy x N` (equivalently `binaryDiscrepancy x N ≤ 1 - Δ`).
Used in Track B to establish the matching lower bound `1 - D_N(L_f) ≫ (log log N) / (log N)^{1-δ}`.
label: one_sub_discrepancy_ge_of_separated_mass
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.one_sub_discrepancy_ge_of_separated_mass

doc:
Exact single-shape maximum relative length for the primary corner `(1, 1)` of
`α(b, p) α(b, q)` for arbitrary real parameters `p, q > 1` and ratio `r = Q / P > 0`:
`min (((q - 1)/q) * r, (p - 1)/p) / (1 + r) ≤ (p - 1)(q - 1) / (2pq - p - q)`.
label: general_single_shape_one_one_max
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.general_single_shape_one_one_max

doc: Equality in `general_single_shape_one_one_max` is attained at `r = q(p - 1) / (p(q - 1))`.
label: general_single_shape_one_one_attained
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.general_single_shape_one_one_attained

doc:
If `deg : Fin k → ℕ` lists distinct degrees and every nonzero integer polynomial in `α`
whose degree lies in `Set.range deg` is normal in base `b`, then the powers `(α^(deg i))` are
jointly uniformly distributed in `[0, 1)^k`.
label: jointUniform_of_established_degrees
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.jointUniform_of_established_degrees

doc:
Echelon-basis multidimensional Weyl theorem (Phase 17 Track A, Theorem 8): if `P : Fin k → ℤ[X]`
are nonzero integer polynomials with pairwise distinct degrees and every nonzero integer polynomial
whose degree lies in `Set.range (fun i => (P i).natDegree)` is normal at `α` in base `b`, then
`(P_1(α), …, P_k(α))` is jointly uniformly distributed in `[0, 1)^k`.
label: jointUniform_of_echelon_degrees
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.jointUniform_of_echelon_degrees

doc:
Pointwise dual inequality of Track C Theorem 1(a): for any `D`, residue `r`,
nonnegative integer carry `c`, and dual weight `lam ≥ 0`, the indicator that the top bit of
`(r + c) % 2^D` is `1` is bounded above by the indicator `r ≥ 2^(D-1)` plus `lam * c` plus the
linear knapsack weight `max 0 (1 - lam * (2^(D-1) - r))` when `r < 2^(D-1)`.
label: carry_knapsack_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.carry_knapsack_le

doc:
Parity Bonferroni dual inequality (Phase 17 Track C, Theorem 4): for every odd `r = 2m + 1`
and every nonnegative integer `n`, the truncated binomial expansion of `(1 - 2)^n` at degree `r`
is a pointwise lower bound on `(-1)^n`.
label: parity_bonferroni_dual_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.parity_bonferroni_dual_le

doc: Kernel-checked verification of the 57-vector `(3, 31)` minimized cyclic-descent orbit.
label: descent31Check_true
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.descent31Check_true

doc:
For every finite binary word `w`, running the minimized `(3, 31)` cyclic-descent automaton from
any orbit state stays inside `descent31Orbit` and ends with first coordinate nonzero modulo `31`.
label: descent31_all_words_nonzero
name: NormalityChecker.Phase17DiscrepancyBounds.descent31_all_words_nonzero

doc: A complete group of `h` consecutive powers after position `m`, in any field.
label: geometric_retirement
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.geometric_retirement

doc: **Geometric retirement identity.** `(b-1)/(b^h-1) · ∑_{r=1}^h b^-(m+r) = b^-(m+h)`.
label: geometric_retirement_weight
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.geometric_retirement_weight

doc:
One complete block `(s, s+h]` with constant raw coefficient `c·(b-1)/(b^h-1)` retires to
the single term `c·b^-(s+h)`.
label: block_retirement
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.block_retirement

doc:
**Grouped retirement, finite form.** Along a strictly increasing schedule `n`, any raw
coefficient sequence that equals `c_k (b-1)/(b^(n_(k+1)-n_k)-1)` on the block
`(n_k, n_(k+1)]` has prefix sums equal to the grouped sums `∑ c_k b^-n_(k+1)`. The multipliers
`c_k` are arbitrary, so signs and zero coefficients are allowed.
label: grouped_retirement
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.grouped_retirement

doc: The retirement weight of a nonempty group lies in `(0, 1]` for a real radix `b > 1`.
label: retirement_weight_mem
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.retirement_weight_mem

doc:
**Grouped retirement, infinite form.** For a real radix `b > 1`, a schedule starting at
zero and bounded real multipliers, the dense raw series converges absolutely and its sum is the
sum of the sparse grouped series.
label: grouped_retirement_hasSum
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.grouped_retirement_hasSum

doc: The retirement weight is the reciprocal of the repunit.
label: retirement_weight_eq_inv_repunit
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.retirement_weight_eq_inv_repunit

doc: Each raw summand `1/(R_h b^m)` has reduced denominator exactly `R_h b^m`.
label: raw_term_den
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.raw_term_den

doc:
A raw summand of a group of length at least two is never a `b`-adic rational: no radix
shift of it is an integer.
label: raw_term_not_radix
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.raw_term_not_radix

doc: Repunits divide repunits of multiple length.
label: repunit_dvd_of_dvd
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.repunit_dvd_of_dvd

doc: Every prime `r ∤ b` divides the repunit of length `r(r-1)`.
label: prime_dvd_repunit
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.prime_dvd_repunit

doc:
**Infinite raw prime support.** If for every `M > 0` some gap of the schedule is divisible
by `M`, every prime not dividing `b` divides some raw denominator, and the set of primes in raw
denominators is infinite.
label: raw_prime_support_infinite
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.raw_prime_support_infinite

doc: Factorial schedules `t·k!` have a gap divisible by every positive integer.
label: factorial_gaps
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.factorial_gaps

doc: A fraction over `p^e` whose numerator is prime to `p` has reduced denominator `p^e`.
label: den_of_unit_numerator
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.den_of_unit_numerator

doc:
After enough shifts a grouped term with a retained off-radix prime power keeps exactly that
denominator: `b^N/(p^e b^n)` has denominator `p^e` for `N ≥ n`.
label: retained_term_den
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.retained_term_den

doc: The coefficient differs from `u - b^g R` by an integer.
label: programCoeff_sub
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programCoeff_sub

doc:
**Exact state programming.** Every completed state has fractional part equal to its
target.
label: programState_fract
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programState_fract

doc:
**Coefficient denominators.** If the previous state has fractional part `u_k`, the next
coefficient has denominator dividing `den u_(k+1) · den u_k`.
label: programCoeff_den_dvd
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programCoeff_den_dvd

doc: With `u_0 = 0` and every target in `[0,1)`, all coefficient denominators obey the bound.
label: programCoeffs_den_dvd
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programCoeffs_den_dvd

doc:
**Off-radix programming.** If every target denominator is a power of a prime `p`, so is
every coefficient denominator.
label: programCoeffs_prime_power
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programCoeffs_prime_power

doc:
**The state is the shifted prefix.** With gaps `g_(k+1) = n_(k+1) - n_k` of a monotone
schedule with `n_0 = 0`, the state `R_L` equals `b^(n_L) ∑_{k<L} c_(k+1) b^-n_(k+1)`.
label: programState_eq_prefix
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programState_eq_prefix

doc:
**Programmed orbit states.** The radix shift of the `L`-th prefix by its own last
insertion exponent has fractional part `u_L`.
label: programmed_prefix_fract
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programmed_prefix_fract

doc:
**Retained denominator.** A completed state has the same reduced denominator as its
target; on an active interval with `u_k = 1/p^(e_k)` the state keeps exactly `p^(e_k)`.
label: programState_den
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programState_den

doc:
**Retired states.** A zero target makes the completed state an integer, so the programmed
prefix contributes nothing modulo one at that insertion.
label: programState_retired
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programState_retired

doc:
**Programmed dense series.** Replacing each programmed term `c_(k+1) b^-n_(k+1)` by its
complete geometric group gives a dense, absolutely convergent series with positive raw
coefficients whose sum is the programmed number.
label: programmed_dense_hasSum
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.programmed_dense_hasSum

doc:
Concentration near integers bounds the discrepancy deficit. The interior arc
avoids all good points, including samples at either end of the closed neighborhood.
label: discrepancy_deficit_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_deficit_le

doc: One-sided finite comparison obtained from the sharp translation law.
label: discrepancy_add_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_add_le

doc:
**Discrepancy transfer theorem.** For every real `x`, `z`, every `ε ≥ 0` and `N > 0`,
`|D_N(x+z) - D_N(x)| ≤ 2ε + E_N(ε)/N`, with `D_N` the extreme interval discrepancy over
half-open subintervals of `[0,1)` and `E_N(ε)` the number of positions `n < N` at which
`b^n z` is farther than `ε` from every integer.
label: discrepancy_transfer
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_transfer

doc:
**Asymptotic transfer.** If `E_N(ε)/N → 0` for every `ε > 0`, the discrepancies of `x+z`
and `x` differ by `o(1)`; in particular their upper and lower limits coincide.
label: discrepancy_transfer_tendsto
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_transfer_tendsto

doc: Integer translation leaves every radix shift unchanged.
label: shift_add_int
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.shift_add_int

doc: A `b`-adic rational `A/b^K` leaves every shift from position `K` onward unchanged.
label: shift_add_radix_rat
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.shift_add_radix_rat

doc: `E_N(0) ≤ K` whenever every shift `b^n z` with `n ≥ K` is an integer.
label: farCount_le_of_eventually_int
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.farCount_le_of_eventually_int

doc:
**Eventually integral transfer.** If `b^n z ∈ ℤ` for all `n ≥ K`, then
`|D_N(x+z) - D_N(x)| ≤ min(1, K/N)`. This covers every `b`-adic rational and every finite sum
of eventually integral contributions.
label: discrepancy_eventually_int
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_eventually_int

doc: `E_N(0) ≤ K` for the `b`-adic rational `A/b^K`.
label: farCount_radix_rat_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.farCount_radix_rat_le

doc: **Finite `b`-adic transfer.** `|D_N(x + A/b^K) - D_N(x)| ≤ min(1, K/N)`.
label: discrepancy_radix_rat
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_radix_rat

doc: Integer translations preserve the discrepancy at every cutoff.
label: discrepancy_add_int
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.discrepancy_add_int

doc:
**Integer head, small tail.** If the insertions with index below `K` lie at or before `n`
and the next lies at `m_K > n`, then `b^n ∑ A_k b^-m_k` is within `2B b^-(m_K-n)` of an
integer, where `|A_k| ≤ B`.
label: sparse_near
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.sparse_near

doc:
**Counting far positions.** If `2B b^-w ≤ ε`, every position at which a sparse
perturbation is farther than `ε` from an integer lies in one of the windows of length `w`
before an insertion, so `E_N(ε) ≤ w · #{k : m_k < N + w}`.
label: sparse_farCount_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.sparse_farCount_le

doc:
**Sparse discrepancy transfer.** For a sparse integer perturbation with `|A_k| ≤ B` and any
`w` with `2B b^-w ≤ ε`, `|D_N(x+z) - D_N(x)| ≤ 2ε + w · #{k : m_k < N+w} / N`.
label: sparse_discrepancy_transfer
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.sparse_discrepancy_transfer

doc: Quadratic insertion positions `(k+1)(k+2)` below `M` number at most `⌊√M⌋`.
label: quadratic_insertions_le
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.quadratic_insertions_le

doc:
**The flagship sparse perturbation** `Z = ∑_{k≥1} 2^-(k(k+1))`. For every real `x`,
cutoff `N > 0` and window `w`,
`|D_N(x+Z;2) - D_N(x;2)| ≤ 4·2^-w + w·⌊√(N+w)⌋/N`; the choice `w ≍ log₂ N` gives
`O(log N/√N)`.
label: quadratic_sparse_transfer
name: NormalityChecker.Phase18Synthetic.quadratic_sparse_transfer

doc: **Lemma 0.1 (positive side):** a nonnegative fractional part below `b^(-L)` forces `L` zero digits.
label: digits_eq_zero_of_fract_lt
name: NormalityChecker.Phase22Cores.digits_eq_zero_of_fract_lt

doc: **Lemma 0.1 (negative side):** a fractional part above `1 - b^(-L)` forces `L` digits `b - 1`.
label: digits_eq_top_of_fract_gt
name: NormalityChecker.Phase22Cores.digits_eq_top_of_fract_gt

doc: Multiplicativity of `dirichletOneConv χ` on coprime arguments.
label: dirichletOneConv_mul_of_coprime
name: NormalityChecker.Phase22Cores.dirichletOneConv_mul_of_coprime

doc: Prime-power evaluation of `1 * χ` for any completely multiplicative `χ : ℕ → ℤ`.
label: dirichletOneConv_prime_pow_of_completelyMul
name: NormalityChecker.Phase22Cores.dirichletOneConv_prime_pow_of_completelyMul

doc:
Explicit local prime-power nonnegativity of `1 * χ` for real completely multiplicative
functions taking values in `{-1, 0, 1}` (Proposition 1.1 local factor).
label: dirichletOneConv_prime_pow_nonneg_of_realMul
name: NormalityChecker.Phase22Cores.dirichletOneConv_prime_pow_nonneg_of_realMul

doc:
**Proposition 1.1 (Track A3): nonnegativity of `1 * χ` for completely multiplicative real characters.**
If `χ : ℕ → ℤ` is completely multiplicative (`χ 1 = 1`, `χ (a * b) = χ a * χ b`) and takes values
in `{-1, 0, 1}`, then `0 ≤ dirichletOneConv χ n` for every `n : ℕ`.
label: dirichletOneConv_nonneg_of_realMul

**Dominant-loss `p`-adic coincidence peeling lemma (Track C1 / C3-M1).**
Let `p` be prime and `d ≥ 1`. Suppose `y_i = a_i / p^(h_i)` (`i ∈ s`) has a unique top loss
`h_top = h j₀ ≥ 1` with `p ∤ a j₀`, and `w_i = c_i / p^(g_i)` (`i ∈ t`) has `p ∤ c i` for all
`i ∈ t` and total loss `∑ i ∈ t, g i < 2 * h_top`. If
`∑ i ∈ s, (a i / p^(h i))^d = ∑ i ∈ t, (c i / p^(g i))^d`,
then there is a **unique** `i₀ ∈ t` with `g i₀ = h_top`, and every other `i ∈ t` has `g i < h_top`.

name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.shifted_tail_tendsto_zero

many phases vanish. Each zero phase occupies a whole interval of proportional length.

name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.normal_iff_eventually_nonzero

Interval counts on nonzero shells are uniform, with error measured relative to
the full prefix length. The same cutoff works for every interval and partial shell.

name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.nonzero_shells_uniform

remainder can put the fractional part near one.

name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.zero_shells_miss_interior

doc:
**Lemma 1.1 (exact margins).** For `b ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ m ≤ b - 2`, and any `L`, the interior fixed
point `c_m = m / (b - 1)` lies in the cylinder of `m^L` with exact left and right margins
`m / ((b - 1) b^L)` and `(b - 1 - m) / ((b - 1) b^L)`.
label: interior_fixed_point_margins
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.interior_fixed_point_margins

doc:
**Lemma 1.1 (interior fixed-point margin).** For `1 ≤ m ≤ b - 2` and any `L`:
1. `1 / ((b - 1) b^L) ≤ η_{m,L}`;
2. every `t ∈ [0, 1)` within circle distance `r < η_{m,L}` of `m / (b - 1)` lies in the
   cylinder of `m^L`, i.e., `⌊b^L t⌋₊ = m * repunit b L`.
label: interior_fixed_point_margin
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.interior_fixed_point_margin

doc: **Lemma 1.1 (interior fixed points).**
label: floor_eq_repunit_of_near
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.floor_eq_repunit_of_near

doc: **Lemma 1.2 (the boundary fixed point).**
label: floor_eq_zero_or_top_of_near
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.floor_eq_zero_or_top_of_near

doc:
**Lemma 2.2 (localization; strict form).** If `b ≥ 2`, `N ≥ 3`, and
`1 - D_N(x; b) < δ ≤ 1/2 - 1/N`, then there is a fixed point `c_j = j / (b - 1)` (`0 ≤ j ≤ b - 2`)
such that at most `δ N` shifts `n < N` lie at circle distance `> b δ / (b - 1)` from `c_j`.
label: exists_fixed_center_of_deficit
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.exists_fixed_center_of_deficit

doc:
**Lemma 2.2 (localization; exact non-strict deficit form).**
For `b ≥ 2`, `N ≥ 3`, and `δ = 1 - D_N(x; b) < 1/2 - 1/N`, there is `j` with `j + 2 ≤ b` such that
at most `δ N` shifts `n < N` lie at circle distance `> b δ / (b - 1)` from `j / (b - 1)`.
label: exists_fixed_center_of_deficit_le
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.exists_fixed_center_of_deficit_le

doc: **Theorem 3.2 (finite dichotomy; strict form).**
label: word_dichotomy_of_deficit
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.word_dichotomy_of_deficit

doc: Helper: `m * repunit b L` is distinct from `0` and `b^L - 1` when `1 ≤ m ≤ b - 2` and `L ≥ 1`.
label: mul_repunit_ne_boundary
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.mul_repunit_ne_boundary

doc:
**Theorem 3.2 (exact exclusive finite digit dichotomy).**
Let `b ≥ 2`, `L ≥ 1`, `N ≥ 4`, and `δ = 1 - D_N(x; b) < b^{-(L+1)}`. Then exclusively either:
1. **(boundary)** `otherWordFreq b L x N ≤ δ`, and no interior `m` satisfies `1 - wordFreq m^L ≤ δ`;
2. **(interior)** there is a unique `m` with `1 ≤ m` and `m + 2 ≤ b` such that
   `1 - wordFreq b L x (m * repunit b L) N ≤ δ`, and `otherWordFreq b L x N > δ`.
label: finite_digit_dichotomy
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.finite_digit_dichotomy

doc:
**Corollary 3.3 (quantitative finite failure of simple normality).**
For `b ≥ 3`, `N ≥ 4`, and `δ = 1 - D_N(x; b) < b^(-2)`, some base-`b` digit `d < b` has
frequency at most `δ / (b - 2)`, hence deviates from `1 / b` by at least `1/b - δ/(b - 2)`.
label: exists_digit_freq_le_of_deficit
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.exists_digit_freq_le_of_deficit

doc:
**Theorem 3.4(d) / Corollary 3.3 (no simple normality in `K_b` for `b ≥ 3`).**
For every integer base `b ≥ 3` and every `x ∈ K_b` (`D_N(x; b) → 1`), `x` is NOT simply normal
in base `b`.
label: not_simply_normal_of_mem_kernel
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.not_simply_normal_of_mem_kernel

doc:
**Binary kernel transitions vanish.** For every `x ∈ K_2`, the frequencies of the length-2
binary words `01` (`v = 1`) and `10` (`v = 2`) both tend to `0`.
label: binary_transitions_tendsto_zero_of_mem_kernel
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.binary_transitions_tendsto_zero_of_mem_kernel

doc:
**No 2-normality in the binary kernel `K_2`.** For every `x ∈ K_2`, the length-2 words
`01` and `10` have frequency tending to `0`, so `x` is not 2-normal (and hence not normal in base 2).
label: not_two_normal_of_mem_binary_kernel
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.not_two_normal_of_mem_binary_kernel

doc:
For every base `b ≥ 2` and every `x ∈ K_b`, the length-2 non-constant word `0(b - 1)`
(value `b - 1`) has frequency tending to `0`.
label: wordFreq_transition_tendsto_zero_of_mem_kernel
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.wordFreq_transition_tendsto_zero_of_mem_kernel

doc:
**No normality in `K_b` (Theorem 3.4(d)).** For every base `b ≥ 2`, no element of `K_b`
is normal in base `b`.
label: not_normalIn_of_mem_kernel
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.not_normalIn_of_mem_kernel

doc:
**Theorem 3.4(a–c) (asymptotic classification in `K_b`).**
Every `x ∈ K_b` satisfies a single alternative valid for every word length `L ≥ 1`:
- **(boundary)** `otherWordFreq b L x N → 0` and `wordFreq b L x 0 N - digitFreq b x 0 N → 0`
  for every `L ≥ 1`;
- **(interior)** for a unique `m` with `1 ≤ m` and `m + 2 ≤ b`,
  `wordFreq b L x (m * repunit b L) N → 1` for every `L ≥ 1`.
label: kernel_eventual_dichotomy
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.kernel_eventual_dichotomy

doc: **Lemma 5.1 (integer head + oriented tail decomposition).**
label: pow_mul_coeffSeries_eq_int_add_tail
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.pow_mul_coeffSeries_eq_int_add_tail

doc: **Lemma 5.1.** `{b^n F_b(a)} = {T_n}` for every absolutely convergent integer coefficient series.
label: shift_coeffSeries_eq_fract_tail
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.shift_coeffSeries_eq_fract_tail

name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.shift_eq_fract_tail

label: orientedTail_succ
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.orientedTail_succ

doc: **Theorem 5.2(a) (positive side).** If `0 ≤ T < b^(-L)`, then `{T}` reads `0^L`.
label: floor_fract_eq_zero
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.floor_fract_eq_zero

doc: **Theorem 5.2(a) (negative side).** If `-b^(-L) ≤ T < 0`, then `{T}` reads `(b - 1)^L`.
label: floor_fract_eq_top
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.floor_fract_eq_top

label: otherWordCount_le_badTailCount
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.otherWordCount_le_badTailCount

doc:
**Theorem 5.2(c) (finite oriented-tail bound for `0^L`).**
Among the first `N` starts, the count of `0^L` differs from `#{n < N : T_n ≥ 0}` by at most
`badTailCount b a L N`.
label: wordCount_zeros_sub_posTail_le
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.wordCount_zeros_sub_posTail_le

doc:
**Theorem 5.2(c) (finite oriented-tail bound for `(b - 1)^L`).**
Among the first `N` starts, the count of `(b - 1)^L` differs from `#{n < N : T_n < 0}` by at most
`badTailCount b a L N`.
label: wordCount_maxDigit_sub_negTail_le
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.wordCount_maxDigit_sub_negTail_le

doc:
**Sharp local-support shadow bound.** The number of shifts `n < N` with a nonzero coefficient
in `(n, n + L]` is at most `L * (1 + S(N - 1))` (using only support points `≤ N - 1` plus at most
one trailing shadow window for the first support point `≥ N`).
label: nearSupport_card_le_succ
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.nearSupport_card_le_succ

doc:
**Theorem 5.3 (general shifted-tail bad-tail bound).** For every `b ≥ 2`, summable `a`, and
`N, L, k : ℕ`,
`badTailCount b a L N ≤ (L + k)(1 + S(N - 1)) + b^L * ∑_{n < N} shiftedTail b a n (L + k)`.
label: badTail_card_le_of_shiftedTail
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.badTail_card_le_of_shiftedTail

doc:
**Theorem 5.3 (linear-mass bad-tail bound).** Under `absMass a X ≤ C * X`, for all `N, L, k`:
`badTailCount b a L N ≤ (L + k)(1 + S(N - 1)) + C * (N + L + k + 2) / b^k`.
label: badTail_card_le_linear_mass
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.badTail_card_le_linear_mass

doc:
**Proposition 6.1 (gap-exact tail scaling).** Across a gap of `g - 1` zero coefficients
`a(n + 1) = ... = a(n + g - 1) = 0`, `T_n = T_{n + g - 1} / b^(g - 1)`.
label: orientedTail_of_gap
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.orientedTail_of_gap

doc:
**Lemma 6.2(b) (strict geometric tail bound).** If `|a(n + 1 + j)| ≤ H` for all `j` with
strict inequality for at least one `j`, then `|T_n| < H / (b - 1)`.
label: abs_orientedTail_lt
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.abs_orientedTail_lt

doc:
**Lemma 6.2(c) (sign determination under dominance).** If `|T_m| < |a(m)|`, then
`a(m) + T_m > 0 ↔ a(m) > 0`.
label: sign_of_dominant
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.sign_of_dominant

doc:
**Corollary 6.4 (bounded coefficients with `H ≤ b - 1`).** If `|a(m)| ≤ H ≤ b - 1` for all `m`
and `a` is not cofinally nonzero (infinitely many zero coefficients), then
`badTailCount b a L N ≤ L * (1 + S(N - 1))`.
label: badTail_card_le
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.badTail_card_le

doc:
Under linear coefficient mass `A(X) ≤ C * X` and density-zero support `S(N) / N → 0`,
the bad-tail frequency `B'_L(N) / N` tends to `0` for every word length `L`.
label: badTailFreq_tendsto_zero_of_linear_mass
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.badTailFreq_tendsto_zero_of_linear_mass

doc:
**Theorem 6.7 (asymptotic oriented-tail transfer).**
1. For any fixed `L ≥ 1`, if `badTailCount b a L N / N → 0`, then `wordFreq(0^L) - posTailFreq → 0`,
   `wordFreq((b-1)^L) - negTailFreq → 0`, and `otherWordFreq → 0`.
2. If `badTailCount b a L N / N → 0` for every `L ≥ 1`, then `coeffSeries b a ∈ K_b`.
label: asymptotic_oriented_tail_transfer
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.asymptotic_oriented_tail_transfer

doc:
**Corollary 7.1 (nonnegative sparse series read almost exclusively `0^L`).**
For every base `b ≥ 2` (including `b = 2`), every nonnegative integer sequence `a : ℕ → ℤ`
(`∀ m, 0 ≤ a m`) with linear mass `absMass a X ≤ C * X` and density-zero support `S(N) / N → 0`,
and every word length `L : ℕ`, the frequency of `0^L` in `coeffSeries b a` tends to `1`.
label: nonneg_sparse_zeros_tendsto_one
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.nonneg_sparse_zeros_tendsto_one

doc:
**Corollary 7.1 (non-simple-normality in EVERY base `b ≥ 2`, including base `2`).**
Any nonnegative integer sequence with linear mass and density-zero support produces a number
that is NOT simply normal in base `b` (including `b = 2`).
label: not_simply_normal_of_nonneg_sparse
name: NormalityChecker.SimpleNormalityKernel.not_simply_normal_of_nonneg_sparse

doc:
**Lemma 8.0 (odd-weighted Beatty sum).** For every real `α` and `K : ℕ`,

observables (for example, all intervals). The cutoff and errors may depend on the support.
label: transfer_clean_blocks
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.transfer_clean_blocks

doc:
Finite Lambert-to-Taylor head reindexing: for any rational weight sequence `a`,
summing `a m * ∑_{r=1}^{⌊N/m⌋} 2^{N - m*r}` over `1 ≤ m ≤ N` equals the binary-level
head `∑_{n=1}^N (∑_{m | n} a m) * 2^{N - n}`.
label: lambert_head_eq_taylor
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.lambert_head_eq_taylor

doc:
Exact prime-band identity in the Lambert head: for every prime `p` with `N/2 < p ≤ N`,
the single Lambert term `a_p * 2^{N - p}` differs from the Taylor term `2^{N - p} / p`
by the integer `-2^{N - p}`.
label: lambert_prime_band_mod_one
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.lambert_prime_band_mod_one

doc:
Non-cancellation at the largest prime factor: if `p` is prime and every prime `q ∈ S`
satisfies `q ≤ p`, then `p` does not divide `∏ q ∈ S, (q - 1)`. In particular, for `m ≥ 2`
and `p = P^+(m)`, `p` never cancels from the denominator of `a_m = (1/m) ∏_{q|m} (1 - q)`.
label: largest_prime_not_dvd_prod_sub_one
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.largest_prime_not_dvd_prod_sub_one

doc:
Local Bernoulli bound for the integer-cleared numerator `g(m) = m a_m = ∏_{p|m}(1-p)`:
for every prime `p` and exponent `e ≥ 1`, `|1 + e * (1 - p)| < p^e`.
label: cleared_local_abs_lt
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.cleared_local_abs_lt

doc:
Parity of the local factor of `(m a_m) * 1`: for every odd prime `p` and `e ≥ 1`,
`1 + e * (1 - p)` is odd (so odd primes contribute zero 2-adic valuation).
label: cleared_local_odd
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.cleared_local_odd

doc:
At `p = 2`, the local factor `1 + e * (1 - 2) = 1 - e` vanishes iff `e = 1`,
explaining the exact zero locus `n ≡ 2 (mod 4)` of `(m a_m) * 1`.
label: cleared_local_two_eq_zero_iff
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.cleared_local_two_eq_zero_iff

doc:
Markov 1-bit upper bound for nonnegative integer Lambert series (such as `L_{chi_4}`):
if each position `n ∈ window` has nonnegative unwrapped sum `S n ≥ 0` and bit `1` forces
`1/2 ≤ S n`, then the count of `1`-bits in `window` is at most `2 * ∑ n ∈ window, S n`.
label: nonneg_one_bit_count_le
name: NormalityChecker.WeightedLambertIdentities.nonneg_one_bit_count_le

doc: For each fixed tolerance the small diagonal denominators have upper Banach density zero.
label: small_denominators_uniformly_sparse
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.small_denominators_uniformly_sparse

label: missing_fraction_uniformly_sparse
